passage:
Manoj sat on the balcony of the Andheri flat with his laptop, frowning at a bug that wouldn't go away. Siddharth came out with two mugs of tea and put one beside him. Manoj rubbed his eyes.

"Long day?" Siddharth asked. Manoj nodded.

"Can I?" Siddharth held his hand near Manoj's hair, not touching. "Only if you want it."

"Yes, please."

He ran his fingers lightly through Manoj's hair a few times. Manoj's shoulders dropped and he leaned in a little, eyes closing. After a minute Manoj said, "That's enough, thanks," and Siddharth stopped at once, squeezed his shoulder, and picked up the tea.

qa.q: What did Siddharth bring out to the balcony?
qa.a: Siddharth brought out two mugs of tea.

qa.q: What did Manoj's leaning in and dropped shoulders suggest?
qa.a: They suggested Manoj felt comforted and safe with the touch, after a long day. Manoj also said yes when asked, so the reading is backed by consent, not just by posture.

qa.q: What made this a caring way to offer a gentle touch?
qa.a: Siddharth asked first, kept the hand still until Manoj said yes, and stopped at once when Manoj said enough.

qa.q: What could Siddharth have done if Manoj had stiffened or said no?
qa.a: Siddharth could have pulled back, put the hand down and checked in gently about what Manoj needed instead.

grounding: A gentle stroke of hair conveys tenderness between partners, welcome because consent was asked and respected.

passage:
"Can I sit here?" Maria asked, dropping her bag on the sofa.
"Of course," said Simran. "Bad exam?"
"Awful. I froze on the last question." Maria's voice wobbled. "Is it okay if I put my head on your shoulder for a bit?"
"Sure. Come here."
Simran stroked Maria's hair a few times, slowly. Then Maria's shoulders tensed.
"Too much?" Simran asked, pulling her hand back at once.
"A little. Just sit with me instead."
"Okay. I'm right here."
They watched the rain run down the window for a while. Maria breathed out. "Thanks for checking. Sometimes I want closeness, sometimes I don't."
"I'll always ask," said Simran.

qa.q: What did Maria ask Simran before putting her head on the shoulder?
qa.a: Maria asked, 'Is it okay if I put my head on your shoulder for a bit?'

qa.q: Why did Maria's shoulders tense while her hair was being stroked?
qa.a: Maria felt it was a bit too much at that moment, and needed closeness without stroking. It shows a person can want comfort and still not want every kind of touch.

qa.q: What did Simran do that showed good care?
qa.a: Simran pulled the hand back at once and asked 'Too much?', then simply stayed beside Maria.

qa.q: How might Simran have felt when Maria said 'a little'?
qa.a: Simran may have felt a flicker of worry about having overstepped, but the quick adjustment and the promise to always ask suggest care rather than hurt.

grounding: A caress offers tenderness only with consent, and when a person stiffens, the other stops and checks in.
